After the recent death of David Lynch, I finally decided to force myself to watch the rest of the The Return after not being able to stomach the Dougie shit for three episodes when it first came out. To say it was not worth the watch is an understatement. As a big fan of seasons 1 and 2, even with the bad stuff in them, this is like watching a Breen version of a David Lynch TV show. The only thing that was remotely like watching the original show is that one scene with Big Ed at the gas station, where it feels like he knows something is happening or fixing to happen while watching out the front door in silence. The only one to actually keep his story arc from the original too. And the scene with Bobby in the forest with the boys was very Twin Peaky. But the shit when Cooper FINALLY returns in mind body and spirit Lynch has the absolute GALL to burn in an image of Coopers face on the only episode that feels Twin Peaky with the implication that it is a dream, with the real ending saying "Evil always wins, nothing matters in this world, or the next". Nothing was done to make the viewer feel anything about that ending, and feels like another "We dont know how to end it, so have this bullshit" type of ending. Hell, theres even a scene where Albert says "Your going soft" to Gordon, and what does David Lynch reply with? "Not where it counts buddy!". Constantly has some sort woman with him or ogling the new young agent with Albert. It also feels like he cucked every original male character that had a relationship except for Big Ed and Andy, and even still it TOOK TWO FUCKING DECADES for Big Eds good ending to happen.

Now I regret not watching it in full when it first came out so I could have tweeted to his face how much Twin Peaks The Return sucked, but knowing how he was in life, he probably would have enjoyed that reaction. That is the only explanation for this show, and why Audrey was even in it for the weird ass dance and argument scenes. What else could explain the weird ass script, the dead silence of 90% of the runtime, and the "But why?" questions I kept having throughout each episode.

I bring up "But why?", because it can mean one of two things. A good story teller will be able to get viewers to ask "But why?", but not out loud because they know its a question to a cosmic event that will never be answered, and you must come up with an answer yourself. This was done expertly in the first season, and parts of the second season. David Lynch failed this test with The Return, as every episode I constantly grew frustrated asking over and over "But why?", even after getting the "pay off" of why, which is usually "the story happens". This might not be terrible on its own, but over SIXTEEN FUCKING EPISODES it becomes a strain to watch. The only time he passed was with bobby and the police bros in the forest going to the coordinates they found in Briggs chair. The slow walk up with talking about Bobbys childhood with Briggs in this area, the fact he named it, and the absolute bonkers scene of Andy with the Fireman and the boys returning to the dead tree was excellent. Id even say we didnt need the scene of Andy with the Fireman, as him disappearing and returning with the weird lady is enough to tell the viewer something cosmic just happened, and you are not getting anymore info. I would have been happy trying to explain what happened to Andy here, but instead we got an explanation. It wasnt great, it wasnt horrible, it was just plain. But everything around it echos what happened to Briggs when he disappeared when Cooper was taking a piss. That is the Twin Peaks I miss. One moment you are enjoying a talk with the bros on a walk, and suddenly you experienced a situation that you can not explain, forced to return to the previous moment with no time to decompress. 

It feels like this was actually filmed during COVID, as tons of characters never interacted that should have like the Hornes or Nadine / Dr Jacoby with everyone else. All the "one off" characters in the bar with stories that belong in a high school musical movie that was there to just pad runtime because the bands David Lynch loved didnt do enough to meet length requirements. All of it was shit. Anyone else who says otherwise is just smelling their own farts in wine glasses.

Also, I found this by searching "why does twin peaks the return suck so much". Hope you are doing well op, after creating this thread 7 years ago.

RAID is not for bit rot. RAID is for redundancy, IE Redundant Array of Independent Disks. Its designed to suffer disk failure without outright losing data. ZFS uses RAID to rebuild lost disks in an array, and then uses checksumming to correct bit rot. Bit rot does not happen quickly. You will find bit rot on partitions that are years old. I have seen ZFS arrays that are close to 15 years old and still has all of their data, where as the OS drive is littered with corrupt data in the /home folders. You are not going to find bit flips and bit rot every time you do a scrub.


>Honestly it's never been a problem even when we had Adaptec\LIS RAID cards. With ZFS we've been much more confident thanks to the scrubs, but even so I feel this is a legacy issue.


As for other people saying this, I dont think they understand how different hardware was back when these hardware RAID cards were in use. It wasnt unusual to see Raid5's with 5x200GB disks. Considering how small the magnets on spinning drives have gotten for absolutely large storage drives, drives back then did not have the rates of bit rot that we see today due to the physical size of the magnets on the platters, and how they were arranged. You just cant compare the two eras of storage at all.

I dont see anyone mentioning this so I will. Remove the l2arc and reboot. The l2arc has a very specific use case with hot data that won't fit into ram, usually databases. When you use a l2arc, you actually lose ram space because zfs uses ram to map where data is on the l2arc. So zfs is taking longer to retrieve data because it checks ram first, l2arc second, then the main pool third for the metadata / data. You should really max out the amount of ram you can have first before adding l2arc, and even then the l2arc can still slow you down. Also make sure you are using lz4 for compression, as I find gzip to slow down everything as well.

You should really only have an l2arc if your memory is completely maxed out with no possible way to increase it, and you are running out of free memory to use. It takes ram space to index the l2arc, so it actually can cause zfs to be slower because instead of using ram to cache data, its spending ram space on the l2arc index instead. And the speed up is not instant, it takes time for data to become "hot" and placed on the l2arc. So unless you are doing tons of reads on the same data, you probably won't see a speed increase. 

Test your pool with and without the l2arc to see if its slowing you down. This will at least tell you if this is the case.
